setup.title: How to set up
setup.step1: Download the agent binary for your operating system above, or use the npx command.
setup.step2: Click "New agent" below, give it an identifiable name (e.g. João's Laptop — Client A VPN) and click Create.
setup.step3: Copy the generated token. It is shown only once — store it somewhere safe.
setup.step4: Run the agent on your machine using the copied command. On Windows, run the .exe from PowerShell or CMD; on Linux/macOS, run the binary from a terminal after chmod +x.
setup.step5: Return to this screen: a green icon means the agent is connected. Your SSH sessions will automatically route through it.

help.title: Help: SSH Sessions
help.subtitle: Use this reference to interpret the fields, routes, and diagnostics in the list.

diagnostic.title: 1. Check diagnostic
diagnostic.description: It summarizes whether the session is active, closed normally, or failed.

route.title: 2. Check route
route.description: Shows whether access was direct or went through an Agent.

status.title: 3. Confirm status
status.description: Separates a still-live session from a session already closed.

user.title: User
user.description: Person who opened the SSH session in NodeAccess.

host.title: Host
host.description: SSH host accessed and IP registered in the inventory.

startEnd.title: Start / End
startEnd.description: Times when the session opened and closed.

duration.title: Duration
duration.description: Time between start and end. Active sessions do not have a final duration yet.

route.title: Route
route.description: Actual path used to reach the host SSH service.

diagnostic.title: Diagnostic
diagnostic.description: Operational reason for the state or failure. Hover to see the technical message when available.

status.title: Status
status.description: Indicates whether the session is still active or already closed.

routes.direct: The backend connected directly to the host.
routes.user_agent: The connection went through the Agent bound to the user.
routes.tenant_agent: The connection went through a tenant shared Agent.

normal.label: Closed normally
normal.description: Terminal or WebSocket closed without a recorded connection error.

AGENT_REQUIRED.label: No Agent online
AGENT_REQUIRED.description: The host requires an Agent, but no compatible Agent was online.

AGENT_REQUIRED_USER.label: No user Agent
AGENT_REQUIRED_USER.description: The host requires the user's own Agent, but it was not online.

AGENT_CONNECT_FAILED.label: Agent cannot reach host
AGENT_CONNECT_FAILED.description: The Agent was online, but could not open TCP to the host.

HOST_KEY_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED.label: Host key pending
HOST_KEY_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED.description: The SSH key presented by the host must be verified before access.

SSH_BASTION_CONNECT_FAILED.label: Bastion failed
SSH_BASTION_CONNECT_FAILED.description: The connection failed at the jump server/bastion.

SSH_TARGET_CONNECT_FAILED.label: Host failed
SSH_TARGET_CONNECT_FAILED.description: The route reached the destination, but the final SSH connection failed.

SSH_CONNECT_FAILED.label: SSH failed
SSH_CONNECT_FAILED.description: Generic failure while establishing the SSH connection.

CREDENTIAL_ERROR.label: Credential unavailable
CREDENTIAL_ERROR.description: The required credential could not be resolved.
